summary: Six transitions that turn the shots in 3D (Flip, Cube, Swing, Doorway, Revolve, Push in depth) now sit after the flat ones in the tiles, the Type menu and right-click Add Transition, each with Length, Curve, Direction and Motion blur. A title part, or its words one at a time, can come in by Swing In, Flip Up, Fly In From Depth or Tilt Settle, and go out the same ways.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording and drop a second recording onto the timeline right after it, so two clips meet.

try.do: Open the Transitions section in the panel and scroll its tiles: the six new ones play their move after Blur through.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right-click the second clip and choose Add Transition, Cube.
Click the ruler right on the cut: the two shots are faces of a box half way round.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

Click the title, choose Headline in the Part menu, and set Part In to Swing In: the words swing up one after another.

evaluate: Does each of the six read as a different move when you play it, or do Swing and Revolve look too alike?
Is 0.8 seconds on Ease in out the right starting length and curve for a 3D transition?
Should Motion blur start on for the 3D transitions, given it costs up to three times the drawing time?
Do the doorway's doors leave the frame too quickly, before you see them open?
Do Swing In and Tilt Settle by word feel like a produced title, or too slow to land?
rough: No mock covers the six new tiles or the Direction and Motion blur rows; they follow the existing tile and panel row patterns (UX-PATTERNS §4).

Cube matches the depth mock's cube (Pivot depth to the box's middle, Rotation Y 0 to 90, Depth backing off a little at the midpoint); it backs off far enough that the face coming round shows its front, so the box is about 60 percent of the frame at its middle.

Each move is measured at its midpoint in 2026-10-11-depth-reel-numbers.json: every transition shows a picture turned 20 degrees or more and corners travelling 180 to 630 points in 100 ms; the title entrances are turned 20 to 27 degrees at their midpoint. Tilt Settle meets the bar only on its gentle Ease in out sine curve, so a quicker curve makes it barely tilt half way.
Measured at 1080p with ten layers mid transition: 5.0 to 6.0 ms median a frame. With Motion blur on, 6 to 16 ms median, and a slowest frame up to 59 ms, so blur can drop frames while scrubbing.
Depth of field from the camera reaches transitions and whole parts, but not single words or letters coming in one at a time.
Flip Up hides each word until it passes edge on, so the first part of its length shows nothing; with an angle under 90 the part shows tilted before its in starts.
The title restyle walk already failed its last step before this work (a dropdown scrolled under the title bar): task the-title-restyle-walk-reaches-its-last-part-in.
